checks: Complete ordered worker manifests and independent executed-case union must agree; skipped, missing, duplicate or failed cases cannot pass.
One host executor lock serializes complete core jobs; an independent nonblocking flock regression proves the lock is held until work ends.
Every client has a private PID namespace, UID10001, readonly checkout, no Docker socket, 2GiB memory-plus-swap cap and bounded payload tmpfs; combined local working-memory stop is 7GiB.
Client helpers stop before physical PostgreSQL teardown; injected monitor failure preserves reports and restores signal handlers.
Passed volume deletion requires exact nonce-derived name, labels, original creation identity and no running or stopped container references.
Timed-out report readers can remove only the exact owned helper ID; foreign labels refuse deletion.
Fresh nonce builders have inspected 2GiB/no-swap and two-CPU limits; cleanup targets only that builder.
Failed payloads and capacity roots remain durably exported; symlinks are retained without following them and special files cannot block export.
Persistent capacity-directory removal checks UID, mode, nonce, inode and quarantined identity after dependent finalizers.

default_seed_refresh.excluded: Every sampled/rehearsal database and files directory
default_seed_refresh.verdict: ACCEPT only if stale, via existing seed.drop/create

limits: This verdict authorizes only owned local test/seed cleanup, with no production change or global prune.
Full regression, final timing and real sample rebuild receipts are separate gates.
reviewer: root agent, independent of pg_engine and pg_dev authors
scope: Local test supervisor ownership, cleanup, resource limits and failure retention; not a core timing acceptance
